result.title: Physical Laws without Physics Loss? Probing Learned Dynamics in Video World Models through Forced Response
result.summary: Do video world models learn physical laws without a physics loss, or merely imitate motion? Overall motion and appearance scores cannot settle it. We investigate this through nonlinear forced response: an excitation shakes the support of a suspended object. We introduce dual visual-numeric conditioning and adapt six image-to-video backbones to predict this motion using only the flow-matching loss. Wan predicts motion accurately and generalizes to unseen excitations, objects, poses, and scenes. Counterfactual tests suggest capabilities beyond replaying training videos. But what laws have they learned? We design three tiers of tests using Taylor expansions of the dynamics and geometry. All six reproduce the linear response, including resonance; five capture higher-order dynamics, including nonlinear softening. Remarkably, softening is barely present in training: only 0.74% of the swing's squared displacement. Extensions to a double pendulum and a rocking block show sustained dynamics are learned more faithfully than brief impacts. Yet learned dynamics may fail to appear when state estimation or propagation goes wrong. We turn these tests and findings into strategies to improve video training and generation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用受迫响应实验（激励悬吊物体支撑）配合视觉-数值双条件，在仅用 flow-matching loss 的情况下改造六个图像到视频骨干，检验其能否预测未见的激励、物体与位姿，并以基于 Taylor 展开的三级测试区分线性响应、共振与高阶非线性动力学（如软化），最后扩展到双摆与摇摆块。
AI.relevance_reason: 其受迫响应、反事实测试与分阶动力学探针，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留任务必要的物理量，以及状态估计与传播失败如何导致内部推理偏离，可作为诊断表示与状态更新的方法线索。
